title: Fix the padded-bag lines
prompt: The warehouse packs order lines for products `P005` and `P006` in a padded bag when there are at least two of them. The function below was written for that, but it returns the wrong lines. Fix `solve(order_items)`.
rules: A line goes in a padded bag when `product_id` is `P005` or `P006` and `quantity` is at least 2 (2 itself counts).
A line with a missing product or quantity isn't packed this way.
Return every column of `order_items`, unchanged, duplicates included.
hints: Press Run and compare the result with the expected rows: some `P005` lines with a quantity of 1 are there.
Python works out `&` before `|`, so the quantity check only applies to `P006`. The two product checks need their own pair of parentheses, or one `isin`.
"At least 2" is `>= 2`; `> 2` loses every line with exactly two items.
explanation: The starter has two bugs. First, `&` is worked out before `|`, so it reads as "P005, or (P006 with a big quantity)": every `P005` line comes back, whatever its quantity. Grouping the product checks fixes that, and `isin` is the neatest way: `order_items.filter(F.col("product_id").isin("P005", "P006") & (F.col("quantity") >= 2))`. Second, `> 2` means three or more, and the rule is at least two, so it must be `>= 2`. Writing `((F.col("product_id") == "P005") | (F.col("product_id") == "P006")) & (F.col("quantity") >= 2)` gives the same rows.
